first words: The problem is with example-based testing
hook title: Example-based testing is just generating evidence
youtube description (first paragraph): With example-based testing, you're never actually proving that this is correct under all possible inputs or conditions. You're just generating evidence. Let's say you do 10 examples, and then 10 more examples trying to think of weird edge cases. There's no proof here. No mathematical proof, no logical proof, just evidence.

first words: With Lean, you write a proof
hook title: With Lean, if it compiles, the proof is right
youtube description (first paragraph): With Lean, you write propositions, you write a proof, and you combine that with a name into a theorem. Lean will check it for you automatically. If it doesn't compile, the proof is wrong. If it compiles, the proof is right. So you can basically have AI generate the proof.
